title: Massive Wildfire Engulfs Glesvær, Sotra
text:
A dangerous wildfire is currently threatening homes south of Sotra, Norway , rapidly spreading across Glesvær and Kausland , prompting emergency response . This article details the ongoing efforts to contain the blaze, potential evacuation plans, and the challenges faced by firefighters. Learn about the current situation and the measures being taken to protect residents.

Wildfire threatens Homes South of Sotra, Norway
Wildfire Threatens Homes South of Sotra, Norway A important wildfire erupted Wednesday in the Glesvær and Kausland area, south of Sotra, Norway, prompting a large-scale emergency response. The blaze,consuming grass and heather,rapidly spread across the landscape,raising concerns for nearby residences and cabins.
Photo: Arne Ristesund initial Response and Challenges emergency services were dispatched promptly, but as of 10:30 p.m. local time, the fire remained uncontrolled. Casper Kaland , the police chief on-site, reported that the fire had two distinct fronts and was moving southward across the island.
The challenging conditions prompted authorities to call in the Civil Defense. A helicopter stationed in Rogaland was placed on standby for deployment Thursday morning,though it does not fly in the dark, according to Børre Brekkvassmo,acting guard commander at the 110 Central Vest.
Evacuation Assessments and Road Closures Several roads, including Glesnesvegen, were blocked due to the fire, creating a difficult situation for residents. Authorities are considering potential evacuations.
Tatiana Knappen, operations manager in the Western Police District, stated at 10:30 p.m. that We still haven’t got control of the fire out there. Efforts are being done so that this does not spread south, towards Glesnes, where there is more buildings. Knappen added that the police were in contact with the Øygarden municipality’s emergency guard regarding possible evacuation measures.
Protecting Structures and Calming Winds Firefighters initially focused on preventing the fire from reaching nearby cabins and houses. Fortunately,these efforts appear to have been successful.
These cabins are now cleared.The wind has calmed down a bit on the spot, so it’s good, Brekkvassmo at the 110 central reported.
Photo: Arne Ristesund Ongoing Efforts and Long-Term Action Six fire stations are currently involved in extinguishing the blaze, including teams from Øygarden Fire and Rescue, Laksevåg station, and Bjørnafjorden station. A fire boat from Sandviken station is also assisting.
Brakkvassmo indicated that the firefighting operation would be lengthy, stating, The status is that no control has been reported.It goes towards a long -term action.
Resident Accounts and Initial Observations police have confirmed receiving reports of flames affecting grass and heather in the area. Hilde Stubsve Kausland, a nearby resident, reported seeing flames approaching her house, telling reporters, It burns out in the field. I am very stressed.
Extent of the fire and Cabin Concerns Operations manager Tatjana Knappen noted, in the area there are some buildings, which we assume are cabins. The affected area is estimated to span over a hundred meters.
